news.originalContent:
Taliban government hopes its Wakhan Corridor road will open new trade routes and reduce reliance on Pakistan, but Beijing remains wary.

At an altitude of nearly 4,900 metres, at the Wakhjir Pass, Afghanistan ends and China begins. Snow closes the pass for at least five months of the year, and people cross it only sporadically in the months when it is passable.

There is no official border crossing here, and yet, on October 4, Afghanistan’s Taliban-led government celebrated the opening of a road leading to the frontier – but crucially not crossing it.

Afghanistan’s Ministry of Rural Rehabilitation and Development said the road through the Wakhan Corridor in Badakhshan province had been built in two phases for 365 million afghanis ($5.5m).

It is a basic road – an unpaved track covered with gravel. On the other side of the border, there is no Chinese customs facility, and China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not commented on the road’s opening.

For the moment, the road leads to a closed border, with no indication of when Beijing might open it to commercial traffic.

The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow protruding stretch of land extending for about 350 kilometres (220 miles). It lies between Tajikistan to the north and Pakistan to the south, but is entirely within Afghan territory, connecting it with China.

The corridor’s unusual shape was determined by the competition between Britain and Russia over the region in the 19th century. An agreement between the two powers in 1895 delineated Afghanistan’s northern boundary with Russian territories (that now make up modern-day Tajikistan), and left Wakhan under Kabul’s control to separate the Russian-controlled land from British India.

China was not a party to the conflict, however, and Kabul and Beijing did not settle the border until 1963.

The area – on both sides of the border – is remote. But in recent years it has gradually become one of Asia’s most sensitive geopolitical crossroads, where China’s security concerns, Afghanistan’s economic ambitions, the interests of Pakistan and Iran, and Central Asian countries’ regional connectivity projects intersect.

As competition intensifies over trade and logistics routes across Asia, this narrow corridor could take on a role far beyond its geographical limits: a potential link between South, East and Central Asia, and a key to reshaping patterns of trade and influence in the region.

Serious discussion of a road through Wakhan began in June 2009, during discussions between the Afghan and Chinese governments.

However, the project went no further than preliminary studies at the time, with the corridor’s rugged terrain cited as a major obstacle to implementation.

The Chinese press at the time also noted concerns over national security, particularly that Uighur fighters could use the corridor as an entry point into China.

The project was frozen until 2019, when Afghanistan began building a road in Wakhan, according to former Afghan ambassador to China, Javid Qaem.

Sixty kilometres (37 miles) were completed, “but the sudden change of government in Afghanistan in August 2021 led to the plan being postponed”, Qaem told Al Jazeera, in reference to the Taliban takeover.

Former Afghan acting defence minister, Shah Mahmoud Miakhel, who served in the position in 2021 and left a few months before the Taliban took power, told Al Jazeera that “the presence of [United States] and foreign forces and the security situation” prevented the road project from being implemented.

“Beijing considered those circumstances to be limiting the prospects for developing the corridor,” Miakhel said.

The Taliban government, however, picked up the project in the years since, making it one of its strategic projects while strengthening political and diplomatic contacts with Beijing.

It hopes to turn the corridor from an isolated border area into a gateway connecting Afghanistan to Chinese and Central Asian markets and strengthening its position in regional trade networks.

“The Taliban resumed construction of the Wakhan road in September 2023, seeking financial support from China to build this future trade route, but China has not yet agreed to open its border with Afghanistan because of security threats,” Qaem said.

In January 2024, the Taliban announced that the road had reached the Chinese border. In March 2025, the rural development ministry signed a contract with local companies for a second, 71-kilometre (44-mile) phase. The authorities say the project was funded from Afghan government resources, and the available information does not indicate any Chinese funding.

In August 2025, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi – the most senior Chinese official to visit Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power – made his second visit to Kabul since the takeover.

In his meeting with Afghan Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani, Wang said China “supports the early resumption of bilateral patrols in the Wakhan Corridor to maintain peace and tranquillity in the border areas”. He also called on Kabul to crack down on the East Turkestan Islamic Movement, a Uighur separatist group.

Unlike Afghanistan, China does not view the Wakhan Corridor primarily as an economic project, but as a highly sensitive security issue. Beijing’s priorities in Afghanistan fall into three main areas: protecting its western border, preventing armed groups from entering Xinjiang (East Turkestan), and safeguarding its investments in natural resources, as well as protecting the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.

An Afghan government source, who requested anonymity, offered Kabul’s account of China’s position.

“China does not oppose opening its border with Afghanistan through the Wakhan Corridor, but it links implementation of the project to the availability of effective security guarantees,” the source told Al Jazeera. The source said that the Taliban had demonstrated their ability to maintain security and secure the border.

The question of Xinjiang, considered by the Uighur people to be their homeland, is therefore the apparent priority for China when it comes to Wakhan.

A 2022 United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights report condemned the “arbitrary detention of Uighurs and other Muslims in Xinjiang”. China has rejected the findings, describing them as part of a Western campaign against it.

Beijing continues to proceed cautiously when it comes to Afghanistan. Major Chinese investments have stalled. In June 2025, the Taliban cancelled an oil exploration contract in the Amu Darya Basin with a Chinese company, saying it had failed to fulfil its obligations. And in May of this year, Afghanistan’s mining minister complained to the Chinese ambassador about delays in the Mes Aynak copper mine project, which has yet to begin production.

China shares land borders with 14 countries and maintains extensive economic and trade relations with most of its neighbours. But Afghanistan, alongside Bhutan, remain the only countries bordering China that have yet to benefit from a direct overland crossing for trade.

Kabul wants Wakhan to provide a route that is not controlled by Islamabad. Afghanistan is landlocked, and its routes to the sea run through Pakistan and Iran. Over the past year, both routes have been all but closed at the same time.

Mohammad Ismail Ghaznawi, who was governor of Badakhshan before becoming deputy minister of public works for road maintenance in August, said the Wakhan road project was “part of the government’s plan to diversify trade outlets and reduce dependence on Pakistani border crossings”, and referenced fighting between Afghan and Pakistani forces that has been ongoing this year.

Ghaznawi added that the US-Israel war on Iran also directly affects Afghan trade, making the opening of alternative routes a priority.

The Afghan government views the road as the beginning of a trade corridor, and perhaps a railway in the future, that would connect the country to China’s Belt and Road Initiative and generate transit fees.

“The corridor should not be viewed simply as a crossing connecting Afghanistan and China, but as a strategic corridor that could serve as a link between South Asia and Central Asia, strengthening regional trade and economic integration and contributing to security, stability, and development in the region,” Ghaznawi said.

Even as the Afghan side lauds the Wakhan road project as an alternative to dependence on Pakistan, China is not acting as though it is looking for an alternative.

Beijing continues to call for the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor to be extended into Afghanistan and has not opened the Wakhjir Pass. A gravel road closed by snow for months cannot replace a major crossing such as Torkham, through which a significant share of Afghanistan’s trade with Pakistan used to pass.

Miakhel, the former Afghan defence minister, also linked recent security tensions in Badakhshan to the corridor project, saying there were “attempts to obstruct its completion”.

He added that he believed “regional and international parties do not want closer ties between Afghanistan and China amid the geopolitical changes taking place in the region”.

As for Iran, the government there is looking for overland routes to reduce its dependence on the sea and sees a possible road-and-rail corridor through Afghanistan to China as a potential strategic shift in its foreign trade.

Former Afghan ambassador to Iran Abdul Ghafoor Liwal told Al Jazeera that Iran “sees the Wakhan Corridor as a strategic opportunity to strengthen its overland connection with China through Afghan territory”.

Badakhshan does not appear as peaceful as the Afghan government suggests. In May 2024, the province saw rare protests against campaigns to destroy poppy fields.

And in recent months, the opposition National Resistance Front has claimed responsibility for several attacks in the province. Hours after the road-opening ceremony, the group announced that it had killed the deputy head of Taliban intelligence in Faizabad, the provincial capital.

Miakhel linked tensions in Badakhshan to the corridor project, saying: “There are attempts to obstruct its completion.” He believes regional and international actors do not want closer relations between Afghanistan and China, while emphasising that this is his personal assessment.

The future of Wakhan will remain dependent on whether the parties concerned can reconcile security requirements with economic considerations. If they succeed, the corridor could be transformed from an isolated mountain strip into one of Asia’s most important trade links over the coming decades. But if security concerns and regional competition persist, Wakhan will remain a symbol of great geographical potential that has yet to be realised.

news.originalTitle: FAA grounds all fights across the US over ‘telecommunication outage’
news.title: FAA grounds all fights across the US over ‘telecommunication outage’
news.originalSummary:
FAA grounds all fights across the US over ‘telecommunication outage’

The FAA has issued a ground stop for departing flights in the US after a communications failure disrupted air traffic control. The Homeland Security secretary says the shutdown was a precautionary measure as officials investigate further. It’s unclear when flights will resume.

منبع تصویر، Secretary of War Pete Hegseth/X

پیت هگست، وزیر دفاع آمریکا، به سرباز نگهبانی که هنگام بازدید او و همراهانش از گورستان ملی آرلینگتون به آنها تذکر داده بود سکوت و احترام را رعایت کنند، مدال اهدا کرد.

در ویدیویی از مراسم روز کهنه‌سربازان آمریکا در ۱۱ نوامبر که در شبکه‌های اجتماعی خبرساز شد، هگست به همراه همسر و شماری از مشاوران ارشد خود در مقابل مقبره سرباز گمنام عکس یادگاری می‌گرفتند.

پس از گرفتن عکس، صدای صحبت و خنده برخی از حاضران شنیده می‌شود و سرباز نگهبان با صدای بلند به آنها تذکر می‌دهد: «همه بازدیدکنندگان باید در تمام اوقات فضای سکوت و احترام را حفظ کنند.»

یک روز بعد، پنجشنبه ۱۲ نوامبر، هگست در مراسمی در پنتاگون به توماس ایگلسیاس، سرباز ارتش آمریکا، مدال «تقدیر خدمات مشترک» اهدا کرد.

پنتاگون اعلام کرد این مدال به پاس «انجام وظایف او در مقبره سرباز گمنام» اهدا شده است.

در عکس‌هایی که در حساب کاربری هگست در شبکه اجتماعی ایکس منتشر شده، او در حال نصب مدال بر سینه ایگلسیاس و دست دادن با این سرباز دیده می‌شود.

نظامیان دیگری نیز در مراسم اهدای مدال حضور داشتند که پنتاگون آنها را از اعضای هنگ سوم پیاده‌نظام ارتش آمریکا، معروف به «گارد کهن»، معرفی کرده است. این هنگ مسئولیت نگهبانی و انجام تشریفات در مقبره سرباز گمنام را بر عهده دارد.

هگست در توضیح عکس‌های منتشرشده نوشت: «ما سربازان را دوست داریم. ما به معیارها پایبندیم. آفرین، سرباز متخصص. به کارتان ادامه دهید، میهن‌پرستان.»

شان پارنل، سخنگوی ارشد پنتاگون، در واکنش به انتشار ویدیوی تذکر نگهبان گفته بود: «در جریان بزرگداشت این روز مهم، یک سرباز به‌درستی و با احترام به همه یادآوری کرد که آداب مراسم را رعایت کنند.»

او افزود: «وزیر دفاع و تمام این وزارتخانه همواره فداکاری‌های مردان و زنان نیروهای مسلح آمریکا را که برای حفظ امنیت این کشور انجام داده‌اند، ارج نهاده‌اند و خواهند نهاد.»

مقبره سرباز گمنام در گورستان ملی آرلینگتون، از مهم‌ترین یادمان‌های نظامی آمریکا، محل دفن بقایای سربازان گمنام این کشور از جنگ‌های جهانی اول و دوم و جنگ کره است.

از سال ۱۹۴۸، نیروهای هنگ سوم پیاده‌نظام ارتش آمریکا به‌صورت شبانه‌روزی نگهبانی از این مقبره را بر عهده داشته‌اند.

منبع تصویر، AFP via Getty Images

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

بر اساس مقررات گورستان ملی آرلینگتون، بازدیدکنندگان باید با صدای آهسته صحبت کنند و از هرگونه رفتار اخلال‌گرانه یا نامحترمانه بپرهیزند.

به گزارش سی‌بی‌اس نیوز، شریک خبری بی‌بی‌سی در آمریکا، تذکر نگهبانان به بازدیدکنندگان رفتاری غیرمعمول نیست و آنها گاهی چند بار در روز برای حفظ سکوت و احترام به حاضران تذکر می‌دهند.

پیش از این ماجرا، دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، جی‌دی ونس، معاون او، و شماری دیگر از مقام‌های ارشد دولت در مراسم سالانه گذاشتن تاج گل در گورستان ملی آرلینگتون شرکت کرده بودند.

ترامپ در سخنرانی خود از نظامیانی که برای آمریکا جنگیده‌اند قدردانی کرد و از آنچه موفقیت دولتش در جنگ با ایران می‌داند، سخن گفت.

او همچنین از عملکرد هگست در مقام وزیر دفاع تمجید کرد و گفت که او «کار فوق‌العاده‌ای» انجام داده است.

یک روز پیش از مراسم روز کهنه‌سربازان، تلاش برای استیضاح هگست در مجلس نمایندگان آمریکا بر سر نقش او در آغاز جنگ با ایران بدون مجوز کنگره ناکام مانده بود.

هگست این تلاش برای استیضاح را «مضحکه» و «حرکتی نمایشی» توصیف کرده است.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani will announce on Monday the rebranding of the NYPD’s controversial Strategic Response Group as he faces pressure from his lefty allies to ban the elite tactical unit.

Mamdani promised to get rid of the SRG during his mayoral campaign after activists for years complained about the way in which the unit handled protests.

Hizzoner is slated to say he’s “decoupled” the 500-strong police unit’s duties of responding to demonstrations from its counterterrorism tasks, insiders briefed on the plans told The Post.

The hastily cooked-up ploy is meant to appease the far-left wing of his party — which has recently loudly advocated for Mamdani to make good on his campaign promise to disband the SRG, sources said.

Mamdani will pitch the move as a “massive overhaul” of how the city deals with First Amendment-protected gatherings in the city — but insiders claimed the announcement would have little-to-no effect on the ground.

Sources described it as more of a revamp in which the SRG will continue operating under a different name, and still respond to active shooters and other potential mass casualty or terrorism-related events.

“This is not a disband, this a rebrand,” said one city official.

One of the only substantive changes put forward by the administration will be the addition of a slate of civilian workers who will work under the Mayor’s Office of Community Safety, which currently only has two employees.

The workers, who have yet to be hired or trained, will respond to protests to attempt to de-escalate alongside officers in the NYPD’s Community Affairs Bureau, which already responds to the overwhelming majority of demonstrations.

“That is like at least a year out,” one source predicted.

The civilians will not respond to protests without armed officers, according to the insiders.

If protests turn violent, additional officers could be called in to make arrests, but it wasn’t immediately clear from which units.

The SRG historically has responded to demonstrations when they turn violent and can only be deployed with the sign off of the mayor. It has only handled such events fewer than 20 times this year and made around a dozen arrests.

Mamdani additionally plans to announce a ban on kettling — a police tactic to encircle protesters, which became controversial during the 2020 George Floyd protests — and tear gas.

Both are already being banned in the patrol guide.

The attempt at a splashy move comes after his comrade, congresswoman-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier, attacked the Mamdani administration over the handling of a protest after ICE agents shot a Dominican migrant in the city.

She pushed for the SRG to be disbanded, setting off a firestorm among fellow Democratic Socialists of America members, who joined the calls.

Mamdani campaigned on the pledge but after taking office, the complicated process was not prioritized.

He put the project on the “back burner,” and then scrambled to come up with a response to the backlash, The Post reported last week.

The announcement is not expected to be an executive order, sources said.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The state’s education chief is pushing Gov. Kathy Hochul and Albany pols to cough up an expected massive funding increase for school districts to comply with her controversial move to KO the Regents.

The tin-cup pitch from Commish Betty Rosa could trigger a battle with Hochul, who has been critical of phasing out the state’s Regents exams, which New York high school students have been required to pass to graduate.

“When we have an initiative like this, we can’t be starved,” Rosa said during a Board of Regents meeting this week, referring to her push to replace the exams with alternative graduation requirements — and the need to train teachers to achieve her demand.

“This state has to make a huge investment if we’re going to modernize and transform education,” she said without specifying how much money she would request from Hochul and the state legislature.

Her department declined to comment to The Post.

The Regents exams, which students have needed to pass in math, English, science and Global Studies to obtain a diploma, became a graduation requirement during former Gov. George Pataki’s tenure and under then-state Education Commissioner Richard Mills.

The Board of Regents, with Rosa’s backing, voted in September to make the exams optional — meaning kids wouldn’t have to take them if they didn’t want to — as the panel worked to develop alternative graduation requirements that could include student projects or portfolios.

But the federal government recently stepped in and is requiring the kids to at least still take the exams, regardless of what New York does with the results, according to the Albany Times Union.

Beginning in 2028, New York high school students will no longer be required to pass the exams to finish high school.

The state’s graduation policy is set by the 17-member New York Board of Regents, whose members are appointed by Democrats who control the legislature.

The governor does not have a direct role in appointing the Regents, but Hochul has enormous power over school funding and has passed laws she wanted that impact education, such as banning cellphones during the school day.

“The Governor’s priority remains ensuring all New York students receive a high-quality, rigorous education,” a Hochul rep said in an emailed response to Rosa’s comments. “Details of the Executive Budget will be released in January.”

The Times Union first reported that Rosa would seek additional state funding to help establish new graduation standards and train educators to implement them.

Teachers across the state will need experts to instruct them on how to grade portfolios and other projects students must pass for graduation, a more challenging task than easy-to-grade Regents exams.

Rosa said every school may need a coach to help master the new graduation standards.

“We can’t keep using the excuse, ‘They’re not ready,’” Rosa said of districts.

Last year, the Regents board requested a $1.1 billion increase in school funding for various projects.

Hochul said she should have more say over education policy, including graduation requirements. But the education department is not under her purview.

Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

“People see in the articles, ‘New York state abandons Regents,’” Hochul said recently on the Max Politics Podcast. “They think I’m New York.

“The buck should stop with me, given that we are the funder of education.”

Hochul’s fellow Democrats control the Assembly and Senate, and she would have to wage a potentially nasty fight with them to stop or reverse the Regents board’s decision to scrap state exams as a graduation requirement, sources said.

Pataki, governor from 1995 to 2006, told The Post in September that “getting rid of the Regents is incredibly stupid.

“It seems like the Education Department’s main function right now is to disguise the fact that too many New York state schools are failing to educate our kids,” the former gov said.

news.originalContent:

Mayor Zohran Mamdani crowed Friday that New York City now complies with the state’s mandate to reduce public school class sizes — but it only happened after he begged for an extension and his administration tweaked the math.

Hizzoner and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels announced that 73.4% of Big Apple public school classes now comply with the class-size law, “surpassing” the 70% compliance target for the 2026-27 school year.

The law requires all New York City classrooms to have no more than 20 to 25 students, depending on grade level, by the 2029–30 school year.

The limits are set at 20 students for K-3rd grade, 23 for grades 4 to 8 and 25 for high school.

The Mamdani administration successfully pushed for a two-year extension after Samuels admitted in March that the mandate would be “very difficult” to meet by the 2027–28 school year.

The state also reduced the compliance target this year to 70%, down from the original target of 80%.

In addition to the decreased target and extension, which weren’t mentioned in City Hall’s self-congratulatory press release, the city also quietly changed its math to hit compliance.

On page seven of the Department of Education’s report, it admits that this year’s count included “cluster” classes — like gym, music or tech classes that aren’t taught by their usual teacher.

“NYCPS updated its data reporting capabilities and infrastructure to include cluster classes to further support compliance with the law,” the November report states.

Without the tricky tweak, the Big Apple would have only hit a 69.5% compliance rate under previous years’ counts, Samuels told Chalkbeat, which first reported the news.

The report also states that exam prep courses at the middle and high school level were added into this year’s count.

Meanwhile, despite Hizzoner’s administration bragging about its $244 million investment to hire teachers to comply with state law, the Big Apple has 500 fewer teachers than last year’s total of 69,900.

Enrollment in New York City public schools plummeted by nearly 22,000 last year alone in its steepest decline since the pandemic, according to an October Comptroller report.

The Big Apple has lost a whopping 187,000 students since the 2013-14 school year, the comptroller report also found.

City Hall and the NYC Department of Education did not respond to requests for comment.

Los Angeles City Hall turned into an ’80s nostalgia fest Friday as punk rock legend Billy Idol and his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens packed the council chamber for a rock ‘n’ roll celebration before taking the party outside for a concert on the Spring Street lawn.

Councilwoman Monica Rodriguez declared Nov. 13 Billy Idol Day in Los Angeles, honoring the British rocker whose spiky platinum-blond hair, signature sneer and rebellious anthems helped define the MTV generation.

“So few artists have left a mark on rock and roll quite like Billy Idol,” Councilwoman Monica Rodriguez told the packed City Hall crowd, praising the punk icon’s decades-long influence on music.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

“If you don’t love the ’80s, something’s wrong with you,” she joked before the packed chamber.

Born William Michael Albert Broad in England, Idol first made his mark in the late 1970s as the frontman of the punk band Generation X before launching a solo career that turned him into an international superstar.

After moving to New York in the early 1980s, Idol teamed up with Stevens, whose blistering guitar riffs helped create the sound behind hits including “White Wedding,” “Rebel Yell,” “Eyes Without a Face” and “Dancing with Myself.”

His music became a fixture on MTV, while albums including Billy Idol, Rebel Yell and Whiplash Smile cemented his place in rock history.

Idol, who has called Los Angeles home since 1987, credited the city with helping him fulfill a childhood dream.

“A large part of my music has been made here, always written here,” Idol told council members. “Los Angeles has helped me to fulfill that.”

The 70-year-old rocker also made clear he has no plans to leave his adopted hometown.

“Some people kept telling me to move, and I’m still here,” Idol joked.

Stevens, a Grammy-winning guitarist who also performed on the Top Gun anthem and Michael Jackson’s “Dirty Diana,” recalled how his partnership with Idol began just nine miles from City Hall.

He remembered Idol knocking on his hotel room door with a demo of “White Wedding,” a song they would soon perform at the Central, the Sunset Strip club later renamed the Viper Room.

“What a great day for rock and roll. What a great day for Billy Idol. Or Billy Effing Idol, as you would say,” Stevens joked.

Idol also poked fun at receiving the honor on Friday the 13th.

“We’re gonna make that lucky,” he quipped.

The celebration then spilled out of City Hall and onto the Spring Street lawn, where Idol and Stevens performed a concert, bringing a blast of rock nostalgia to the heart of Los Angeles government.

news.originalContent:

A plaque honoring the Silicon Valley Denny’s where Jensen Huang famously founded Nvidia in 1993 is now gone – just a day after the chip titan resigned as CEO following reports he had multiple affairs.

The plaque sat above the booth that Huang and two of his co-founders – Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem – occupied when they conjured up what would become the key driver of today’s artificial intelligence boom.

“The booth that launched a $1 trillion company,” the inscription read in all-caps.

Now, only an empty patch of brick wall and chipped paint are left, according to an NBC News report, which noted two employees said the plaque had been removed.

When asked over the phone if Denny’s or someone else had removed the plaque, an employee at the San Jose, Calif. diner told The Post that she couldn’t provide any details.

The plaque was installed during a 2023 ceremony in which Huang – who said he washed dishes and waited tables in a Portland, Ore., Denny’s when he was 15 years old – met with Denny’s CEO at the time, Kelli Valade. They reminisced about Nvidia’s founding story during their confab.

Huang said he and his co-founders met at a booth near the back of the Denny’s to discuss creating a chip that would enable realistic 3-D graphics on personal computers. The Denny’s is roughly 8 miles from Nvidia’s headquarters.

“It had all the coffee you could drink and no one could chase you out,” Huang told Valade, according to an Nvidia blog post about the ceremony.

In the wake of Huang’s exit, passersby left flowers and bags of potato chips — a nod to the semiconductor chips that Nvidia builds – outside the company’s headquarters in Santa Clara, according to reports. Getty Images depicted a man placing a candle in front of an Nvidia sign.

Huang was forced to resign following a torrent of allegations in recent weeks over his conduct while at the helm of Nvidia.

The tech titan fessed last week to an affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, no relation.

Huang also faced allegations that he had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care — an exec who reports to him, the New York Times reported Wednesday.

Reuters reported Thursday that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, citing unnamed sources. Her name and other details were not known.

Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer and executive vice president, is serving as interim CEO. Kress has been with the company for 13 years and will also continue to serve in her current roles during the search for a permanent replacement, which will consider both internal and external candidates.

Dejounte Murray has had enough of New Orleans.

The former All-Star requested a trade from the Pelicans, with his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials beginning to work toward finding him a new home, ESPN’s Shams Charania first reported.

The Pelicans then put out a statement and said they are looking into “potential trade options.”

“Today, Dejounte Murray’s representatives informed us of his request to be traded,” the Pelicans said in a statement shared on X. “We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization.”

The trade request comes less than two days after Murray took to social media to suggest there was “sabotage” going on behind the scenes with the team.

After the Pelicans’ blowout 145-111 home loss to the Nets on Wednesday, Murray took to X, pointing out that the team was 1-8 with him in the lineup this season and 3-0 without him.

“From what’s going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this!! THE ‘SABOTAGE’ IS REAL!!” Murray wrote in the since-deleted post.

Murray, 30, reposted Charania’s report on Friday afternoon.

At least one potential suitor has already emerged.

The Suns have expressed interest in acquiring Murray, per NBA insider Chris Haynes.

Murray has had a disastrous tenure with the franchise since he was traded by the Hawks in July 2024 for a package headlined by Dyson Daniels and two first-round picks.

Daniels has since emerged as one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA, while Murray has appeared in just 54 games in a Pelicans uniform, suffering a fractured hand in his New Orleans debut before tearing his Achilles in January 2025.

The Pelicans, who hired Jamahl Mosley as their head coach during the offseason, have lost four straight games, including a 51-point drubbing at the hands of the Warriors on Monday.

Murray is making $32.8 million this season and holds a $30.8 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign after signing a $114-plus million veteran extension in 2023.

news.originalContent:
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says federal aviation agency is ‘investigating the issue’.

The United States has grounded flights across the country after a “communication issue” impacted traffic control centres, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.

“FAA [Federal Aviation Administration] technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them,” Duffy wrote on social media.

The FAA said in a post on X that there had been a “temporary telecommunications outage” and that, as a precaution, all flights were being halted. International flights would be handled case by case, it added.

About 7,000 flights have been either delayed or cancelled due to the stop, according to FlightAware.

Some 4,042 flights were in the air, heading to US airports, when the ground stop was ordered, according to the tracking site Flightradar24.

The communication issue affects all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which guide aircraft.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters there was no indication that the ground stop was triggered by a threat to the US. “Everybody’s safe. The flights are accounted for,” he said. “This is not another 9/11.”

President Donald Trump had been briefed, he said.

Asked whether a planned rollout of a new AI tool meant to help air traffic controllers could be to blame, Mullin said officials had not ruled it out. “You just can’t rule out anything at this point. We are going through that process,” he said.

The FBI does not believe a cyberattack or criminal activity caused the failure, Bloomberg reported, citing an official familiar with the matter.

The cited official said investigators were examining whether a software update could have caused the outage, though the cause had not been determined.

The disruption is the latest sign of strain on the US air traffic control system, which has ⁠been beset by equipment failures, communications problems and ⁠shortages of controllers, as the FAA tries to replace ageing infrastructure.

Congress approved $12.5bn for the overhaul last year, and the FAA and White House asked lawmakers on Friday for ⁠another $30.1bn.

This is the first nationwide US ground stop since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. Before that, the last time had been after the September 11, 2001, attacks.

The FAA has not provided any indication of when the ground stop might be recalled.

news.originalContent:
The Chicago-born pope was welcomed by huge crowds in the coastal city, on the final leg of his South America tour.

Pope Leo has made an emotional return to his former diocese of Chiclayo in Peru, where large crowds welcomed their former bishop exactly one month after he had lung cancer surgery, and he thanked them for their support during his recovery.

“As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life,” he said.

About 500,000 people gathered for Mass at Pampas de Pimentel, a desert park just outside of Peru’s fourth-largest city, according to estimates from the Vatican, while another million lined his motorcade route.

Before he was elected pope, Leo had spent about two decades working in Peru as a missionary priest and served as bishop of Chiclayo, where he is still known as “Padre Roberto” and where his image is ubiquitous, from 2015 to 2023.

In Chiclayo, a coastal city of about 620,000, Leo earned a reputation for staying close to poor communities during times of crisis, including when the region was hit with devastating floods and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Some had camped overnight to see him, while others walked in the hot sun to avoid bumper-to-bumper traffic to get to the open-air Mass.

As he rode in his popemobile, people in the crowd waved yellow and white Vatican flags and shouted, “The pope is from Chiclayo.”

“What a joy it is to return to Chiclayo,” said Leo at the start of his homily.

Originally from Chicago and formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, Leo also holds Peruvian citizenship and declared the country his homeland on Wednesday.

Peru is the final stop of his 12-day, three-country South America tour, coming after visits to Argentina and Uruguay. Approximately 12 million people have come to see him at public events so far.

Last month, he underwent surgery for lung cancer, amid fears that the trip would have to be cancelled. But doctors have said the cancer was localised, had not spread, and would not require further treatment.

Leo will stay in the Chiclayo area until Sunday, leading eight events, including a private dinner with the priests he oversaw during his time as bishop.

news.originalContent:
The criminal association charge over his alleged role in the collapse of the bank comes a week after his removal.

Paraguayan prosecutors have charged former president Santiago Pena with criminal association over his alleged role in the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, a week after Congress removed him from office.

The prosecutor’s office announced the new charge on Friday, adding to the breach of trust and self-dealing charges already facing Pena, who is being held in pretrial detention at a military facility.

The 47-year-old former leader is accused of using his position to direct millions in government funds to Ueno and concealing or downplaying its financial troubles, despite warnings of risky lending practices, while having financial ties to the bank.

Pena, who entered office in 2023, held a stake in the bank’s holding company until last year.

On Thursday, investigators raided his official residence in the capital, Asuncion. The prosecutor’s office said agents from the economic crimes unit were extracting data and gathering relevant information for the investigation.

Last week, Pena tried to step down as president, but Congress rejected his resignation, instead removing him from office through impeachment. Pena was arrested shortly after his removal.

The collapse of Ueno left customers locked out of their accounts, prompting huge protests across the country as thousands demanded accountability and their money back.

Prosecutors had been looking for missing funds and said on Friday that assets had been located abroad, although they did not specify in which countries. They had previously asked the United States, Luxembourg and Argentina for help locating the missing money.

“The necessary steps are under way to request that they be frozen,” prosecutor Francisco Cabrera told reporters.

Three former central bank officials were also arrested on Friday, accused of having known about Ueno’s issues since late last year.

The bank, which held more than $800m in public funds, grew quickly under Pena’s presidency from a financial technology company into a large firm handling state pensions and the accounts of several government entities.

The credit ratings agency Fitch has placed Paraguay’s sovereign rating on watch for a possible downgrade, which would make it more expensive for the government to borrow money.

On Thursday, the Central Bank said it had returned savings to more than 1.8 million people who had deposited money at the bank.

Following the midterm elections, Republicans face mounting pressure to advance what is being characterized as amnesty for illegal immigrant agricultural workers during the remaining time they control the House.

Having campaigned heavily on cracking down on illegal immigration in 2024, GOP lawmakers now face renewed scrutiny over whether they will follow through on those promises before potentially losing their House majority — or if they will cave to special interests and pass an immigration reform plan that includes some form of amnesty. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: White House Scrambles After Trump Again Floats Amnesty Deal With Democrats)

A bipartisan immigration proposal still simmering on Capitol Hill is once again drawing attention after recent remarks from President Donald Trump and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who have signaled willingness to work with Democrats on immigration reform.

Wrong. The word “amnesty” was never even said in this entire exchange.

The legislation, sponsored by Republican Pennsylvania Rep. Glenn (GT) Thompson, chairman of the House Agriculture Committee, is known as the Securing Agriculture’s Workforce Act of 2026 (SAWA). The bill would in effect grant amnesty to illegal immigrants who work in the agricultural sector.

Introduced by Thompson in June 2025, the legislation remains pending in the House Judiciary Committee, where it awaits further action from Chairman Jim Jordan, the next Republican House minority leader.

AmericanHort, a national horticulture industry association, confirmed to the Caller that it sent a letter to the House Judiciary Committee urging Jordan to work with Thompson to advance SAWA.

The organization, which represents the plant and horticultural industry, has also published the letter on its website, calling on lawmakers to address H-2A wage and program issues following a recent California ruling affecting the Department of Labor’s October 2025 interim final rule.

Thompson’s bill also seeks to address agricultural labor shortages by allowing eligible illegal immigrant farmworkers to obtain special immigration status and legally remain in the U.S. while continuing to work in qualifying agricultural jobs.

Specifically, the legislation would extend eligibility to illegal immigrants who performed at least six months of qualifying agricultural work within the previous two years.

It would also waive certain grounds of inadmissibility, creating a pathway for eligible workers to obtain H-2A visa status and legally remain in the country while continuing to work in the agricultural industry.

Jeremy Beck, co-president of NumbersUSA, and Mark Krikorian, executive director of the Center for Immigration Studies, both told the Daily Caller that the proposal amounts to amnesty for illegal immigrants, arguing that it would grant legal status to individuals based on their prior agricultural employment.

Notably, the Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) defines amnesty as the “granting of legal status to any individual who is in the country illegally.”

Rep. Thompson also expressed optimism about the legislation’s prospects during a panel hosted by the American Dairy Coalition at the World Dairy Expo in Madison, Wisconsin, on Oct. 30, saying he hoped Congress would address both SAWA and the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 during the lame-duck session.

Beck added that the midterm elections offered no indication that voters had abandoned that message, but rather that immigration had taken a back seat to other issues, ranking a “distant third” among the issues influencing the results.

At its core, Thompson’s legislation seeks to address employers’ labor needs by providing a legal workforce for temporary agricultural jobs through the H-2A program.

news.originalContent:
The new White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, is prohibiting executive staffers in the White House from meeting with lobbyists without prior approval, a memo says.

The memo, reported by Politico on Thursday, states that approval must come from the Office of White House Counsel, upending how lobbying has worked in the nation’s capital. (RELATED: Editor Daily Rundown: White House Warns Congress Not To Cross The Line With Subpoenas)

“No President in history has fought more relentlessly, selflessly or courageously for the American People than President Trump,” the memo says, according to Politico. “Following his example, White House staff are expected to dedicate their time unwaveringly to the working people of the nation.”

A dozen GOP lobbyists told Politico that Miller’s preference for relationship-based favors and his loyalty to President Donald Trump will make it increasingly difficult for lobbyists to influence the administration as Trump’s final term continues.

U.S. President Donald Trump departs a roundtable discussion on cybercrime with White House Deputy Chief of Staff and Homeland Security Advisor Stephen Miller (R) in the East Room of the White House on October 21, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images)

“The thing with Stephen is, he’s not someone that a lobbyist goes in and has to crack or try to win over,” a lobbyist with Ballard Partners who has worked with Miller before, Hunter Morgen, told Politico. “He doesn’t operate based on relationships. He operates based on policy outcomes that will advance the president’s agenda.”

Another lobbyist said Miller was “impossible to lobby,” adding that not even the people closest to him have much success.

Many other lobbyists are now rethinking ways to work with the administration, while others attempt to avoid Miller entirely by working with staffers on the White House’s Domestic Policy Council and National Economic Council.

WASHINGTON, DC - JULY 16: White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles (L) and White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller arrive to a bill signing event in the East Room of the White House on July 16, 2025 in Washington, DC. President Trump is signing the HALT Fentanyl Act, which aims to permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as schedule I controlled substances and aid law enforcement in prosecuting trafficking and manufacturing offenses. (Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

This marks a clear difference between Miller and his predecessor, Susie Wiles, who went out of her way to maintain relationships with lobbying groups after working within the industry herself.

A Wiles spokesperson agreed, telling Politico that she “understood the importance of having strong relationships” and that Trump is “a very relational person.”

A White House spokesperson told Politico that “President Trump’s loyalty is to the American people, not lobbyists. His team is dedicated to advancing the President’s agenda, not the agenda of D.C. lobbyists. All of the White House components continue to work in lockstep to implement President Trump’s America First agenda.”

هال تنها شرکت‌کننده آفریقایی نیست که با این محدودیت‌ها روبه‌رو شده است. زامبیا به دلیل محدودیت‌های سفر به آمریکا، نماینده خود، پاملا موبانگا، را از این مسابقه کنار کشیده است.

شرکت‌کنندگان از ۸ نوامبر برای ثبت‌نام، پرو لباس‌ها و سایر برنامه‌های مقدماتی مسابقه وارد پورتوریکو شده‌اند. این موضوع فشار بیشتری بر هال و دیگر نمایندگان، از جمله نماینده سودان جنوبی، وارد کرده است تا هرچه زودتر ویزای خود را دریافت کنند.

هال گفته است: «طبق برنامه، امروز باید برای شرکت در هفتاد و پنجمین دوره مسابقه دختر شایسته جهان راهی پورتوریکو می‌شدم.»

زیمبابوه یکی از ۱۹ کشوری است که مشمول محدودیت‌های نسبی سفر به آمریکا شده‌اند. این محدودیت‌ها بر اساس فرمان ریاست‌جمهوری شماره ۱۰۹۹۸ وضع شده و از اول ژانویه ۲۰۲۶ به اجرا درآمده است.

بر اساس این مقررات، صدور ویزاهای گردشگری، دانشجویی و تبادل آموزشی و فرهنگی و همچنین ویزاهای مهاجرتی برای شهروندان کشورهای مشمول متوقف شده است. محدودیت‌هایی نیز برای صدور سایر انواع ویزاهای غیرمهاجرتی در نظر گرفته شده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

سازمان برگزارکننده مسابقه دختر شایسته جهان در زامبیا در بیانیه‌ای اعلام کرد که مشکل پاملا موبانگا ناشی از محدودیت‌های سفر است و ارتباطی با شرایط شخصی او ندارد.

در این بیانیه آمده است: «برخلاف مواردی که درخواست ویزای یک شرکت‌کننده به دلیل شرایط شخصی، مدارک یا مشکلات سازمانی رد می‌شود، وضعیت موبانگا به محدودیت‌های سفر وضع‌شده از سوی رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا مربوط است که زامبیا و دیگر کشورهای آفریقایی را تحت تأثیر قرار داده است.»

موبانگا، ۲۵ ساله و پرستار دارای مجوز فعالیت حرفه‌ای، روز ۸ اکتبر به‌عنوان دختر شایسته زامبیا انتخاب شد و قرار بود نماینده کشورش در رقابت‌های جهانی باشد.

در بیانیه سازمان برگزارکننده در زامبیا آمده است که پنج کشور آفریقایی دیگر نیز با مشکلات مشابهی روبه‌رو هستند، اما نامی از این کشورها برده نشده است.

روزیانا هال گفته است که نگرانی دیگر شرکت‌کنندگان آفریقایی را درک می‌کند و چند هفته گذشته را در آفریقای جنوبی برای پیگیری دریافت ویزای خود گذرانده است.

او گفته است: «من تنها کسی نیستم که در چنین وضعیتی گرفتار شده‌ام. بعضی از خواهران آفریقایی من نیز با همین مشکل روبه‌رو هستند و دقیقاً می‌دانم چه شرایطی را پشت سر می‌گذارند.»

نماینده سودان جنوبی در مسابقه دختر شایسته جهان نیز در واکنش به ویدیوی هال، درباره امکان حضور خود ابراز تردید کرده و نوشته است: «احتمال اینکه بتوانیم به مسابقه برسیم، پنجاه‌پنجاه است.»

هال در ویدیوی دیگری که سه روز پیش از آن منتشر کرده بود، گفته بود که همچنان امیدوار است بتواند خود را به پورتوریکو برساند.

او در توضیح این ویدیو نوشته است: «تلاش برای رساندن زیمبابوه به پورتوریکو ادامه دارد.»

قرار است مرحله نهایی هفتاد و پنجمین دوره مسابقه دختر شایسته جهان روز ۲۴ نوامبر در سالن خوزه میگل آگرلوت در شهر سان‌خوان، پایتخت پورتوریکو، برگزار شود.

واشنگتن‌پست و آکسیوس، دستور آقای ترامپ به جی‌دی ونس برای تمرکز بر مسائل داخلی را نشانه عقب‌نشینی از مسیر توافق و ترجیح ادامه فشار اقتصادی توصیف کرده‌اند؛ بلومبرگ نیز این رویکرد را شرط‌بندی بر دوام وضعیتی شکننده می‌داند و هشدار می‌دهد پذیرش بن‌بست، لزوماً به پایان درگیری یا رفع خطر جنگی تازه منجر نخواهد شد.

دونالد ترامپ در مصاحبه با هیو هویت، استفاده دوباره از نیروی نظامی علیه ایران را منتفی ندانست. آقای هویت پرسید آیا برای جلوگیری از تهدید متحدان و کشتی‌های آمریکایی تردید خواهد کرد؛ آقای ترامپ پاسخ داد: «نه. هیچ تردیدی ندارم.» او افزود اگر روند اوضاع تغییر کند، آماده اقدام است.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا مدعی شد واشنگتن کنترل کامل تنگه هرمز را در اختیار دارد و میزان خروج نفت از منطقه از پیش از جنگ بیشتر شده است. او همچنین ادعا کرد آمریکا طی پنج ماه گذشته سربازی از دست نداده است.

آقای هویت سپس پرسید آیا ترامپ حاضر است محاصره را حتی برای ۲۶ ماه، تا فروپاشی حکومت ایران، ادامه دهد. آقای ترامپ تعهد زمانی مشخصی نداد؛ در عوض، با طرح ادعاهایی درباره تورم، پرداخت‌نشدن حقوق سربازان و نابودی توان نظامی ایران، فشار موجود را مؤثر توصیف کرد.

او در پاسخ به پرسشی درباره باقی ماندن حاکمان کنونی ایران تا پایان ریاست‌جمهوری‌اش، گفت: «بله، این شکست خواهد بود.»

آقای هویت پرسید اگر ایران یک مقام ارشد آمریکایی را بکشد، چه اتفاقی خواهد افتاد. آقای ترامپ تهدید کرد: «دیگر مدت زیادی دوام نخواهند آورد.»

دونالد ترامپ از جی‌دی ونس خواسته است توجه خود را از مذاکرات ایران به مسائل داخلی آمریکا معطوف کند. آقای ترامپ معاونش را مأمور تمرکز بر ادعاهای فساد و جرم در شهرها و ایالت‌های تحت اداره دموکرات‌ها کرده است.

به نوشته این رسانه، شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در انتخابات، هزینه سیاسی جنگ را آشکار کرده است. اکنون، در کنار تشدید حملات یا افزایش فشار برای گرفتن امتیاز، پذیرش بن‌بست نیز مطرح شده است.

نیت سوانسون، مقام پیشین آمریکایی، معتقد است دولت گزینه مطلوبی ندارد: اقدام نظامی خطر تشدید درگیری دارد و چشم‌انداز توافق مناسب نیز ضعیف است. در مقابل، یک مقام کاخ سفید، محاصره، تحریم‌ها و عملیات «دروازه آهنین» را نشانه قدرت موقعیت واشنگتن می‌داند.

گزارش هشدار می‌دهد ادامه این وضعیت می‌تواند متحدان خلیج فارس را مقابل ایرانی جسورتر، بدون مسیر روشن ثبات، باقی بگذارد

دونالد ترامپ می‌گوید عربستان سعودی، قطر و دیگر کشورهای خلیج فارس از او خواسته‌اند فعلاً از حملات گسترده‌تر به ایران خودداری کند و وضعیت کنونی را ادامه دهد. رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در مصاحبه با استیون ای اسمیت در کاخ سفید، مدعی شد می‌تواند به جنگ فوراً پایان دهد، اما به درخواست متحدان منطقه‌ای، فشار اقتصادی و نظامی را حفظ کرده است.

آقای ترامپ گفت: «عربستان سعودی از من خواسته است لطفاً برای مدتی بگذار اوضاع همین‌طور بماند.» او افزود قطر، کویت، امارات متحده عربی و بحرین نیز رویکرد کنونی را ترجیح می‌دهند. با این حال، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا درباره این درخواست‌ها گفت: «مطمئن نیستم با آن موافق باشم.»

وقتی از او پرسیده شد آیا بدون درخواست این کشورها حملات بیشتری انجام می‌داد، پاسخ داد: «بله، انجام می‌دادم.» این پاسخ نشان می‌دهد که به روایت خود او، درخواست متحدان منطقه‌ای در خودداری واشنگتن از حملات گسترده‌تر نقش داشته است؛ هرچند او رضایت کامل خود را از ادامه این وضعیت ابراز نکرد.

آقای ترامپ همچنین تهدید کرد که آمریکا توانایی نابودی زیرساخت‌های انرژی، پل‌ها و تأسیسات تولیدی ایران را ظرف سه روز دارد. او مدعی شد این بخش‌ها تاکنون تا حد زیادی از حملات آمریکا مصون مانده‌اند و گفت: «در یک روز انرژی آنها از بین می‌رود. در یک روز پل‌هایشان از بین می‌رود. و در یک روز توان تولیدی‌شان از بین می‌رود. فقط سه روز وقت می‌برد.»

رول‌کال، رسانه تخصصی سیاست و کنگره آمریکا، تصمیم تازه آقای ترامپ درباره ایران را در چارچوب پیامدهای انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای بررسی کرده است. گزارش جان بنت بر این نکته تأکید دارد که ترامپ تنها نه روز پس از شکست سنگین جمهوری‌خواهان، از بی‌نیازی به توافق برای پایان دادن به درگیری سخن می‌گوید.

به نوشته این رسانه، جنگ و افزایش بهای سوخت و دیگر کالاها، نارضایتی گسترده‌ای ایجاد کرده و حتی بخشی از پایگاه جمهوری‌خواه را به مخالفت کشانده است. آقای ونس نیز پس از انتخابات، جنگ را دلیل شکست حزبش معرفی کرد؛ ارزیابی‌ که آقای ترامپ اصل آن را پذیرفته، اما همچنان از تصمیم خود برای ورود به جنگ دفاع می‌کند.

رول‌کال همچنین ادعای رئیس‌جمهور درباره کنترل تنگه هرمز را در کنار وضعیت این آبراه قرار می‌دهد. گزارش می‌نویسد هرمز همچنان محل مناقشه و برای کشتی‌های تجاری خطرناک است و مقام‌های ایرانی نیز مدعی کنترل بخش عمده آن هستند.

این رسانه تغییر مأموریت آقای ونس به پیگیری ادعاهای فساد در مناطق تحت اداره دموکرات‌ها را تلاشی احتمالی برای جلب رضایت دوباره رأی‌دهندگان جمهوری‌خواه می‌داند. با این حال، اعلام بی‌نیازی از توافق، به‌خودی‌خود پاسخ روشنی به خواست پایان جنگ نمی‌دهد؛ به‌ویژه وقتی ناامنی کشتیرانی و هزینه‌های اقتصادی درگیری همچنان ادامه دارد.

واشنگتن‌پست در گزارش خود، دستور ترامپ به ونس را نشانه عقب‌نشینی از تلاش برای توافق و ترجیح ادامه محاصره دریایی و فشار اقتصادی توصیف می‌کند. به نوشته این روزنامه، آقای ونس برای بررسی امکان پایان مذاکره‌شده درگیری، با تندروهای حکومت ایران وارد تماس شده بود.

گزارش تأکید می‌کند که تغییر موضع آقای ترامپ، ابهام برای متحدان آمریکا در خلیج فارس را افزایش داده است. این کشورها برای حفظ مذاکرات تلاش کرده‌اند و نگران پیامدهای ادامه رویارویی هستند. واشنگتن‌پست تصریح می‌کند هنوز روشن نیست رئیس‌جمهور دیپلماسی را کاملاً کنار گذاشته باشد.

آکسیوس نیز این تصمیم را با تغییر اولویت سیاسی آقای ونس پیوند می‌دهد: معاون رئیس‌جمهور، پس از نسبت دادن شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان به جنگ، اکنون مأمور تمرکز بر ادعاهای فساد در شهرها و ایالت‌های دموکرات شده است.

این رسانه می‌نویسد پیام آقای ترامپ بار دیگر عدم‌اطمینان را به بازارهایی بازگرداند که پایان جنگ را نزدیک تصور می‌کردند؛ قیمت نفت افزایش یافت و سهام افت کرد. آکسیوس همچنین یادآوری می‌کند آقای ونس اخیراً در تلاش برای آتش‌بسی تازه و ازسرگیری مذاکرات هسته‌ای نقش پررنگی داشت.

پرسشی که از کنار هم قرار دادن این دو گزارش شکل می‌گیرد، این است: آیا توقف تلاش علنی برای توافق، تصمیمی پایدار است یا مرحله دیگری از سیاست متغیر واشنگتن؟ هیچ‌یک پاسخ قطعی ارائه نمی‌کنند.

بلومبرگ می‌نویسد دونالد ترامپ رویکرد تازه‌ای را بررسی می‌کند: باقی گذاشتن جنگ ایران در وضعیتی بلاتکلیف و فاصله گرفتن از تلاش برای حل‌وفصل جامع آن. دستور او به جی‌دی ونس برای تمرکز بر مسایل داخل کشور، احتمال پایان درگیری بدون توافق بر سر محدودیت‌های هسته‌ای را مطرح کرده؛ همان موضوعی که توجیه اصلی آغاز جنگ معرفی می‌شد.

به نوشته این رسانه، شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در انتخابات، هزینه سیاسی جنگ را آشکار کرده است. اکنون، در کنار تشدید حملات یا افزایش فشار برای گرفتن امتیاز، پذیرش بن‌بست نیز مطرح شده است.

نیت سوانسون، مقام پیشین آمریکایی، معتقد است دولت گزینه مطلوبی ندارد: اقدام نظامی خطر تشدید درگیری دارد و چشم‌انداز توافق مناسب نیز ضعیف است. در مقابل، یک مقام کاخ سفید، محاصره، تحریم‌ها و عملیات «دروازه آهنین» را نشانه قدرت موقعیت واشنگتن می‌داند.

گزارش هشدار می‌دهد ادامه این وضعیت می‌تواند متحدان خلیج فارس را مقابل ایرانی جسورتر، بدون مسیر روشن ثبات، باقی بگذارد

دونالد ترامپ می‌گوید عربستان سعودی، قطر و دیگر کشورهای خلیج فارس از او خواسته‌اند فعلاً از حملات گسترده‌تر به ایران خودداری کند و وضعیت کنونی را ادامه دهد. رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در مصاحبه با استیون ای اسمیت در کاخ سفید، مدعی شد می‌تواند به جنگ فوراً پایان دهد، اما به درخواست متحدان منطقه‌ای، فشار اقتصادی و نظامی را حفظ کرده است.

آقای ترامپ گفت: «عربستان سعودی از من خواسته است لطفاً برای مدتی بگذار اوضاع همین‌طور بماند.» او افزود قطر، کویت، امارات متحده عربی و بحرین نیز رویکرد کنونی را ترجیح می‌دهند. با این حال، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا درباره این درخواست‌ها گفت: «مطمئن نیستم با آن موافق باشم.»

وقتی از او پرسیده شد آیا بدون درخواست این کشورها حملات بیشتری انجام می‌داد، پاسخ داد: «بله، انجام می‌دادم.» این پاسخ نشان می‌دهد که به روایت خود او، درخواست متحدان منطقه‌ای در خودداری واشنگتن از حملات گسترده‌تر نقش داشته است؛ هرچند او رضایت کامل خود را از ادامه این وضعیت ابراز نکرد.

آقای ترامپ همچنین تهدید کرد که آمریکا توانایی نابودی زیرساخت‌های انرژی، پل‌ها و تأسیسات تولیدی ایران را ظرف سه روز دارد. او مدعی شد این بخش‌ها تاکنون تا حد زیادی از حملات آمریکا مصون مانده‌اند و گفت: «در یک روز انرژی آنها از بین می‌رود. در یک روز پل‌هایشان از بین می‌رود. و در یک روز توان تولیدی‌شان از بین می‌رود. فقط سه روز وقت می‌برد.»

او در همین مصاحبه پذیرفت که افزایش قیمت بنزین ناشی از جنگ، در شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای نقش داشته است. با وجود این اذعان به هزینه داخلی جنگ، همچنان از تصمیم خود برای حمله به ایران دفاع کرد.

رول‌کال، رسانه تخصصی سیاست و کنگره آمریکا، تصمیم تازه آقای ترامپ درباره ایران را در چارچوب پیامدهای انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای بررسی کرده است. گزارش جان بنت بر این نکته تأکید دارد که ترامپ تنها نه روز پس از شکست سنگین جمهوری‌خواهان، از بی‌نیازی به توافق برای پایان دادن به درگیری سخن می‌گوید.

به نوشته این رسانه، جنگ و افزایش بهای سوخت و دیگر کالاها، نارضایتی گسترده‌ای ایجاد کرده و حتی بخشی از پایگاه جمهوری‌خواه را به مخالفت کشانده است. آقای ونس نیز پس از انتخابات، جنگ را دلیل شکست حزبش معرفی کرد؛ ارزیابی‌ که آقای ترامپ اصل آن را پذیرفته، اما همچنان از تصمیم خود برای ورود به جنگ دفاع می‌کند.

رول‌کال همچنین ادعای رئیس‌جمهور درباره کنترل تنگه هرمز را در کنار وضعیت این آبراه قرار می‌دهد. گزارش می‌نویسد هرمز همچنان محل مناقشه و برای کشتی‌های تجاری خطرناک است و مقام‌های ایرانی نیز مدعی کنترل بخش عمده آن هستند.

این رسانه تغییر مأموریت آقای ونس به پیگیری ادعاهای فساد در مناطق تحت اداره دموکرات‌ها را تلاشی احتمالی برای جلب رضایت دوباره رأی‌دهندگان جمهوری‌خواه می‌داند. با این حال، اعلام بی‌نیازی از توافق، به‌خودی‌خود پاسخ روشنی به خواست پایان جنگ نمی‌دهد؛ به‌ویژه وقتی ناامنی کشتیرانی و هزینه‌های اقتصادی درگیری همچنان ادامه دارد.

واشنگتن‌پست در گزارش خود، دستور ترامپ به ونس را نشانه عقب‌نشینی از تلاش برای توافق و ترجیح ادامه محاصره دریایی و فشار اقتصادی توصیف می‌کند. به نوشته این روزنامه، آقای ونس برای بررسی امکان پایان مذاکره‌شده درگیری، با تندروهای حکومت ایران وارد تماس شده بود.

گزارش تأکید می‌کند که تغییر موضع آقای ترامپ، ابهام برای متحدان آمریکا در خلیج فارس را افزایش داده است. این کشورها برای حفظ مذاکرات تلاش کرده‌اند و نگران پیامدهای ادامه رویارویی هستند. واشنگتن‌پست تصریح می‌کند هنوز روشن نیست رئیس‌جمهور دیپلماسی را کاملاً کنار گذاشته باشد.

آکسیوس نیز این تصمیم را با تغییر اولویت سیاسی آقای ونس پیوند می‌دهد: معاون رئیس‌جمهور، پس از نسبت دادن شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان به جنگ، اکنون مأمور تمرکز بر ادعاهای فساد در شهرها و ایالت‌های دموکرات شده است.

این رسانه می‌نویسد پیام آقای ترامپ بار دیگر عدم‌اطمینان را به بازارهایی بازگرداند که پایان جنگ را نزدیک تصور می‌کردند؛ قیمت نفت افزایش یافت و سهام افت کرد. آکسیوس همچنین یادآوری می‌کند آقای ونس اخیراً در تلاش برای آتش‌بسی تازه و ازسرگیری مذاکرات هسته‌ای نقش پررنگی داشت.

پرسشی که از کنار هم قرار دادن این دو گزارش شکل می‌گیرد، این است: آیا توقف تلاش علنی برای توافق، تصمیمی پایدار است یا مرحله دیگری از سیاست متغیر واشنگتن؟ هیچ‌یک پاسخ قطعی ارائه نمی‌کنند.

Camille Fishel shared the emotional moment Fanatics CEO Michael Rubin popped the question.

In the heartwarming video, shared via Instagram Friday, the longtime couple were at a candlelit beachside dinner with their two daughters, Romi, 6, and Gema, 4.

Their little ones shocked their mom by pulling out a hand-painted sign that read, “Will you marry me?,” before Rubin took out the dazzling sparkler and dropped down on one knee Thursday night.

The model also shared a carousel of photos showing Romi and Gema on the beach wearing adorable white tulle dresses.

Other snaps showed Fishel showing off the stunning engagement ring as she cuddled up to her new fiancé.

The family of four celebrated the milestone on the beach as fireworks launched.

Rubin, 54, proposed to Fishel on her 36th birthday after 10 years of dating.

“Happy bday and a little more @camillefishel ❤️😉💍,” the businessman captioned his own post from the lavish engagement.

The exciting announcement drew congratulations from several of the couple’s famous friends.

“Congratulations to the both of you brother!!” NBA great LeBron James posted while NFL legend Tom Brady left three heart emojis.

Rubin and Fishel began dating in 2016. Although it’s not clear how they first met, Rubin made his first appearance on Fishel’s Instagram feed in May of that year.

The Pennsylvania native also has an older daughter, Kylie, 20, from his previous marriage to Meegan Spector. The couple divorced in 2012 after seven years of marriage.

Rubin founded Fanatics, the sports merchandise and collectibles powerhouse, in 1995, and is well known for his connections to some of the biggest names in sports and entertainment.

Nowadays, the billionaire is known for his annual Fourth of July White Party in the Hamptons, which attracts a star-studded guest list.

On Friday, Page Six exclusively reported the details of the entrepreneur’s prenup plans.

A source told us that Rubin will “definitely” have the artist enter into a prenuptial agreement prior to becoming husband and wife.

We’re also told Rubin and Fishel will likely wait until after next year’s Super Bowl in February 2027 to tie the knot.

“I can see them doing a private wedding and then a blowout celebration,” our insider shared. “But they have to get through all his other parties first, including his annual, invitation-only Fanatics Super Bowl Party.”

news.originalContent:

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent let loose on the bloodthirsty Iranian regime Friday — declaring “F the Iranian leadership” after death threats forced him to abandon his $12.5 million Georgetown mansion and relocate to a military base.

“I’m not going to be cowed by the death threats they have made against me,” Bessent declared during a Friday appearance on CNBC’s “Squawk Box,” confirming he had moved under Secret Service instructions.

“The other cabinet members won’t be cowered either,” he added.

Bessent’s relocation was first reported Wednesday, after US officials raised concerns about Iranian threats against his life. The Treasury chief has become a central figure in President Trump’s campaign to financially cripple Tehran through sweeping sanctions.

A senior intelligence officer warned in an unclassified memo last month that Iranian plots targeting US personnel and American citizens have reached an advanced stage.

The severity of the specific threats against Bessent was not immediately clear, and Iran has previously denied plotting attacks against American officials or people on US soil.

Bessent suggested the threats were evidence that Trump’s economic pressure campaign was putting Tehran on its heels.

“What we’re doing is working,” he said, describing Iran as “a dangerous animal backed into a corner.”

“Why am I going to be afraid when our brave military personnel are in the Gulf, President Trump constantly receives death threats?” he added.

The Treasury secretary’s security concerns reportedly intensified after The Wall Street Journal published an aerial photograph of his Georgetown residence in January 2025, following his $12.5 million purchase of the property.

Bessent blasted the newspaper during Friday’s interview, stating his team has asked its editor not to publish the image because it could expose the exact location of his home.

He called the decision “extremely irresponsible and dangerous,” and insisted that “things like this must stop.”

A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that the photograph allowed the property to be geolocated, contributing to growing security concerns surrounding Bessent.

Bessent has been leading Trump’s economic pressure campaign against Iran, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, since August.

The effort has targeted financial institutions and other firms accused of facilitating Iranian transactions, while a US naval blockade of Iranian ports has added to the pressure on Tehran.The administration is seeking to force Iran to end attacks on shipping and reopen the strategically critical Strait of Hormuz, which has been largely closed since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb. 28.

A Treasury Department spokesperson previously told The Post that Bessent would not be deterred by the Iranian regime’s threats and remained committed to the campaign, which the department said was helping collapse Iran’s economy.

Despite the escalating warnings, US officials have acknowledged that Iran’s ability to carry out large-scale attacks inside the US and other overseas territories is limited.

Bessent, meanwhile, made clear he had no intention of backing down.

It wouldn’t be a proper celebration of The View‘s landmark 30th season without an appearance from Candace Cameron Bure. The Full House star co-hosted the Emmy Award-winning talk show for Seasons 19 and 20. During her time on The View, Bure never shied away from sharing her conservative views and willingly engaged in lively debates with her more liberal-leaning co-hosts. The last time Bure appeared on the program was back in 2024.

Any anxiety Bure might have felt about returning to The View was quelled before she stepped on the show’s stage because Bure knew she and the women “weren’t going to talk politics” since they had plenty of other topics to cover. The most important subject was Bure’s recent success on World’s Toughest Test: Special Forces, where she completed the selection process alongside Collin Gosselin and Alexia Umansky. “It’s a huge accomplishment, even though it’s reality TV,” said Bure when she visited the DECIDER studio. “I turned 50 this year. I’m really proud that I hung in there physically and mentally.”

Over the series’ five seasons, only 12 celebrities have completed the course. Out of those 12 celebrities, 8 have been women. After experiencing what these recruits have suffered through on Special Forces, Bure wasn’t surprised at all by that statistic. “You have so many professional [male] athletes that are built and in great shape and yet, often those have been the first people to leave the show,” noted Bure. “I think that [women] have a mental strength that sets us apart, and that’s why so many women endure in this challenge.”

So which one of Bure’s former colleagues on The View was most impressed by her success on Special Forces? “Joy Behar was the most impressed,” revealed Bure. “She couldn’t believe that I was 50!” Along with turning 50 this year, Bure also became a grandmother. Her son, Lev Bure, and his wife, Elliott Bure,  welcomed their son, Bond Leo, back in September. Her daughter, Natasha Bure, recently welcomed a daughter, Winnie Helaine, with her husband, Bradley Steven Perry, this past October.

Bure’s new status as a grandmother came as a shock to Behar as well. “It was blowing her mind that I have grandchildren now,” shared Bure. Bure took Behar’s astonishment as a compliment.  “I adore Joy, I really do,” said Bure.  “It was fun for me.”

Will The View fans have to wait another 2 years to see Bure pay another visit to the show’s iconic table? Given the success of her most recent appearance, we think not!

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

It’s gross, grimy and may be growing somewhere in your bathroom.

Black mold is the stuff of homeowners’ nightmares. It’s notoriously difficult to remove, can cause expensive property damage and has been blamed for a wide range of health problems.

But how worried should you really be about this pesky houseguest? Here’s what you need to know.

There are many different kinds, but when people talk about black mold, they’re usually referring to Stachybotrys chartarum.

This greenish-black fungus occurs naturally in the environment and reproduces through microscopic spores that travel through the air. They can enter your home through open doors and windows, ventilation systems or by hitching a ride on pets, clothing and shoes.

Once inside, the mold can take hold if conditions are right. It thrives in warm, persistently damp environments with access to cellulose — an organic material found in drywall, paper and wood.

That’s why it commonly crops up in water-damaged areas of the home, including basements, bathrooms, laundry rooms and around leaky windows.

It can cause health problems, but it’s not necessarily more dangerous than other household molds, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Like other fungi, black mold can trigger allergies and respiratory problems. Some species, including Stachybotrys chartarum, can also produce mycotoxins — naturally occurring toxins that can be harmful at high doses.

But just because mold can produce toxins doesn’t mean it’ll poison you. Scientists haven’t established that typical household exposure delivers enough mycotoxins to cause the chronic, whole-body poisoning often blamed on “toxic black mold syndrome.”

For some people, mold exposure causes no noticeable problems. Others may develop itchy, red eyes, nasal congestion, sore throat, coughing, wheezing and skin rashes, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

People with asthma, mold allergies or weakened immune systems are more vulnerable to complications, including fungal infections in some cases.

Those exposed to large amounts of mold, such as farmers handling moldy hay, may also experience more severe reactions.

This is where things get murkier.

People living or working in damp, moldy buildings have reported fatigue, headaches, anxiety, depression and cognitive problems, including brain fog and trouble concentrating.

Some animal studies have found that mice exposed to high doses of Stachybotrys spores developed brain inflammation, memory problems and anxiety-like behaviors.

However, major medical organizations point out that no controlled human studies have proven that normal indoor mold levels deliver enough mycotoxins to cross the blood-brain barrier and cause neurological damage.

That said, there are other possible explanations for the psychological symptoms people exposed to mold report.

For example, constant allergies, sinus congestion and asthma flare-ups can disrupt sleep, leaving people exhausted, irritable and mentally foggy.

Dealing with a mold-infested home, worrying about its potential health effects and trying to get to the bottom of unexplained symptoms can also take a psychological toll, potentially worsening existing mental health conditions or contributing to new ones.

“This chronic stressor can lead to heightened anxiety and depressive symptoms, which, in turn, may foster psychosis in susceptible individuals,” according to the Neuroscience Institute.

Damp buildings may also have other irritants, including bacteria and dust mites, that contribute to headaches and other symptoms.

First, tackle the moisture problem. Repair leaky pipes and windows, address water damage and improve ventilation to keep mold from returning.

For smaller patches on hard surfaces, the CDC recommends scrubbing with hot, soapy water or an appropriate commercial mold cleaner. Wear gloves, goggles and an N95 respirator while cleaning.

Moldy porous materials, including carpeting, insulation and drywall, may need to be removed and discarded.

If the mold covers a large area, is growing inside walls or ventilation systems, or you’re experiencing allergic reactions while cleaning, call a professional mold remediation company to help remove it.

In many cases, symptoms improve once the mold is removed and exposure stops.

For people with mold allergies, antihistamines, nasal sprays, decongestants and eye drops can relieve symptoms, according to the Mayo Clinic.

Allergy shots, also known as immunotherapy, may also help some people build up tolerance to specific mold allergens over time.

But before you open your wallet to purchase one of the pricey mold detoxes being hawked online, you might want to think twice.

Medical and toxicology experts say there’s no good evidence that you need a special cleanse to rid your body of mycotoxins from everyday household mold exposure.

Some jewels demand to be seen.

During a conversation at Bucherer‘s Fifth Avenue flagship in NYC this week, celebrity stylist Erin Walsh discussed her work dressing clients like Anne Hathaway and Selena Gomez — and decking them out in diamonds.

While the gown traditionally comes before the jewels, sometimes it’s the other way around; Walsh revealed that she swapped Alison Brie’s look for January’s Golden Globes after finding the most “perfect” Y-shaped diamond necklace from Bucherer.

“I changed the dress for the necklace,” she recalled. “The necklace needed a moment.”

Featuring more than 100 brilliant-cut diamonds set in 18-karat white gold, the “sophisticated” style “drips” down the chest and “looks like it’s part of the body,” as the “Art of Intentional Dressing” author put it.

Along with the necklace (and a matching pear-shaped diamond ring), Brie walked the red carpet wearing a plunging black Anna October gown with sultry ruching and super-skinny straps.

Bucherer’s Art Deco-inspired Baguette Love earrings, meanwhile, have proven to be a perfect pairing for Gomez, who wore them with a white Ralph Lauren pantsuit at the Palm Springs International Film Festival Film Awards in 2025 and with a sparkling red Prada gown at last month’s Rare Impact Fund Benefit.

The logistics of safely shuttling six (or more) figures’ worth of precious stones to and from her superstar clients can be “hilarious,” she said.

“I don’t think people realize, but when I work with Bucherer, walking around, it looks like I either robbed somebody or am in the mafia,” quipped Walsh, who’s also placed pieces on Mindy Kaling and Mariska Hargitay recently.

“I have a very intense black briefcase, and walking into the lobby of the hotel, it’s like [I’m doing] a deal.”

It’s all worth it for the payoff of a perfect red carpet moment, with Walsh saying, “Jewelry is a mood lifter. It ignites something in you. When someone puts on something and they feel great in it, it’s usually pretty obvious.”

There’s one thing you’ll never see on any of her A-listers, though: an even number of rings.

“I learned this from a client many years ago,” she said. “It’s like feng shui, if you think about three, six and nine [considered lucky numbers in Chinese culture].”

Joked Walsh: “I have a disease of ‘more is more.’ If you really love jewelry, wear nine necklaces!”

Britney Spears’ mysterious new business venture has finally been revealed.

The pop superstar’s long-awaited jewelry line, BTiny, launched a new website Friday, just days after Page Six exclusively revealed she was preparing to unveil a “top-secret project.”

A source close to Spears confirmed to Page Six Style that the jewelry collection was the secret venture the singer had spent the past year working on.

Fans who visit BTinyJewels.com are greeted with a message teasing a major announcement.

“Okay so… I’ve been keeping a secret,” the message reads. “A small one … well maybe TINY actually.”

Fans will have to join the waitlist before products are officially announced, and the website hardly gives any hints as to what designs from the Princess of Pop could look like. The logo, however, is rendered in gold and includes a shooting star, hinting at delicate pieces.

On Tuesday, Page Six exclusively reported that Spears, 44, had been quietly preparing to unveil a major new venture, which was a longtime dream of hers.

“For the past year, Britney has been working on a top-secret project,” a source close to the pop star said. “It’s a deeply personal project that both Britney and her fans have longed for for over 20 years.”

“It’s coming very soon!” the insider exclaimed.

news.originalContent:
Stelco’s US owner blames Trump’s tariffs for layoffs, but its support for those same tariffs has raised questions.

Hamilton, Ontario, Canada – Chelsey Masteij had heard layoffs might be coming at Stelco, so she decided to use up some of her vacation days. She was making the most of the time off with her new dog when she got a call telling her not to come back to work.

The 34-year-old had spent years trying to break into the male-dominated steel industry before finally landing a job at the company’s Hamilton plant about three years ago.

She started as a general labourer in the cold-rolling department, later training to operate cranes and taking on shifts in the coke ovens.

The work was gruelling and physically demanding, but Masteij grew to love the routine and the close-knit community of coworkers she came to consider family. When she shared photos of herself with Al Jazeera, all in protective gear at the plant, she joked that she hardly had any pictures outside of work.

Masteij thought she might stay at Stelco until retirement. Instead, she was laid off on October 9.

The news hit hard, and she spent much of the next two weeks sleeping.

“I was in a complete mess,” she told Al Jazeera, her voice cracking as she recalled the experience. “I was kind of depressed.”

Now, instead of working 12-hour shifts, Masteij spends much of her time at home, cutting back on expenses while she collects employment insurance.

Masteij is among hundreds of Canadian steelworkers facing layoffs after Stelco’s American owner, Cleveland-Cliffs, announced in late September that it would temporarily shut down parts of its operations in Hamilton and Nanticoke, Ontario.

Stelco blames the move on United States President Donald Trump’s tariffs, which it says have made it harder to sell Canadian steel to US customers, and on competition from cheaper foreign steel entering Canada.

But government officials and plant workers, including Masteij, are not convinced that is the whole story.

“Right now, there are a lot of lies going on with what’s happened,” Masteij said.

While US tariffs have hurt the Canadian steel industry, the union representing Stelco workers questions whether Cleveland-Cliffs is using difficult market conditions to serve its own business interests, with Canadian workers paying the price.

“Everyone knows we’re being used as pawns, that these layoffs weren’t necessary,” said Ron Wells, president of United Steelworkers Local 1005, speaking to Al Jazeera at his Hamilton office.

In June 2025, Trump doubled tariffs on steel and aluminium imports, including from Canada, to 50 percent, making them more expensive for US buyers.

According to Stelco, Canada’s exports of cold-rolled and coated steel to the US – used to make everything from cars to building materials – fell by 58 percent in the second quarter of 2026 compared with the quarterly average before the trade war.

“When they say that there is less demand for the product coming out of the Hamilton mill, that is correct,” Mang told Al Jazeera.

But it is not just Trump’s tariffs that Cleveland-Cliffs blames for Stelco’s problems.

During a July earnings call, CEO Lourenco Goncalves warned that the company might scale back production in Canada unless Ottawa did more to protect its steel industry from imports.

“And that will have consequences for employment in Canada, but will have a positive financial impact on Stelco and on Cleveland-Cliffs,” he said.

That was the first time Wells had heard jobs might be at risk. The union later offered to help Cleveland-Cliffs lobby Ottawa for stronger protections against foreign steel imports, believing Canadian workers might have more sway with the government.

Instead, the next call brought news of the layoffs.

As of Saturday, 175 workers at Stelco’s Hamilton plant had received layoff notices, with the announced cuts expected to affect up to 500 workers there and in Nanticoke.

Late last month, about 30 attended an information session the union organised in Hamilton, where they could learn about employment insurance and retraining opportunities.

Many were frustrated by the lack of clarity about how long the shutdown would last.

Some asked how their benefits would compare to their wages, while others wondered whether they would qualify for the full amount.

For workers who had spent decades at Stelco, another daunting prospect loomed: having to look for work for the first time in the digital era, competing for jobs with younger applicants as they neared retirement.

Some are already considering heading out west to find work.
